Despite what some headlines may suggest, General Motors (GM) has not changed its stance on CarPlay and Android Auto. The automaker will not be reinstating phone projection features on any of its vehicles that have already had them removed. Here's what's actually going on.

GM has not reversed its decision to abandon CarPlay

The confusion started last week when GM announced a new software experience for its Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks. The company touted a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system, claiming CarPlay and Android Auto would coexist with GM's own infotainment system.

Some media outlets interpreted this news as GM backing down from its plan to drop CarPlay — a plan it first announced in 2023. Unfortunately, that's not the case. GM's original statement was about removing CarPlay support from its future electric vehicles. And aside from the Cadillac Lyriq EV, it has followed through on that plan.

GM has never removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gasoline-powered vehicles. So the new phone projection system in the Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks does not mean the automaker is bowing to pressure and adding CarPlay back to its EVs.

A GM spokesperson confirmed this to Joanna Stern, who posted the following on X today:

The confusion is understandable. GM CEO Mary Barra said in an interview earlier this year that the automaker would remove CarPlay and Android Auto from its gasoline vehicles at some point. The company quickly clarified that gas-powered vehicles would continue to offer phone projection for the "foreseeable future."

Bottom line: nothing has changed. GM is not bringing CarPlay back to its electric vehicles. The strategy remains the same. You could read GM's decision to roll out the picture-in-picture solution for certain gas-powered vehicles as an acknowledgment that dropping CarPlay was unpopular. But I think that's a generous interpretation.

Side note: John Gruber's headline for this news is the best, so I'll give credit where it's due.
